specification.problem: Determine functional equivalence of quantum states and quantum circuits, where complex-valued state vectors admit several notions of equivalence (e.g. exact vs. up to global phase), and design equivalence-checking algorithms that stay fast and robust for circuits with hundreds of qubits, such as quantum communication and search circuits.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of equivalence-checking definitions only. The specific algorithms, data structures and benchmarks are not given in the abstract, so only a small finite illustrative formulation of state and circuit equivalence is provided.

symbols.meaning: unitary matrices of two circuits on n qubits

equations.label: Exact state equivalence
equations.description: Strictest notion: the two state vectors are identical.
equations.abstract_quote: quantum states, which are represented by complex-valued vectors, exhibit subtle differences leading to several notions of equivalence
equations.justification: The abstract says there are several notions of equivalence for vector states; the exact one is the strictest.

equations.label: Equivalence up to global phase
equations.description: Relaxed notion: states differ only by an unobservable global phase.
equations.justification: Standard physics background, taken as one plausible relaxed notion; the abstract does not name it.
assumptions: The paper's relaxed notion is global-phase equivalence

equations.label: Circuit equivalence up to phase
equations.description: Two circuits are equivalent if their unitaries match up to a global phase.
equations.justification: Assumed formalization of the circuit equivalence checking mentioned in the abstract.
assumptions: Unitary circuits with no measurements or ancillas

registers.name: q
registers.role: data qubits on which both circuits U and V act

specification.initial_state: Assumed finite instance: computational basis state |0^n> (or each basis state for full unitary comparison); the abstract gives no initial state.

steps.description: Build the composite circuit V^\dagger U on register q by applying U, then the inverse of V (circuit-level equivalence check, assumed formulation).
Check whether V^\dagger U acts as identity up to a global phase, i.e. is proportional to I.
For state equivalence, compare the output states of the two circuits exactly, then up to global phase.

specification.measurement: Abstract specifies no measurement. Assumed illustration: apply V^\dagger U to |0^n> and measure q in the computational basis; equivalence up to phase predicts outcome 0^n with probability 1 (a necessary check only; for full equivalence repeat over basis or random input states). Equivalent algebraic/symbolic checking would need no measurement.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: declare 'not equivalent' if any shot returns a nonzero bitstring; otherwise report 'equivalent on tested inputs' (statistical evidence only). Global phase is not detectable by measurement, so phase-sensitive (exact) equivalence needs a non-measurement method such as a classical vector or matrix comparison. The paper's actual postprocessing is unknown.
